questions.q: What does NAT (Network Address Translation) primarily do?
options: Encrypts all traffic leaving the network
Lets many devices on a private network share one public IP by rewriting the source IP of outbound traffic
Assigns IP addresses to new devices automatically
Translates domain names into IP addresses
questions.explain: NAT rewrites the source IP (and tracks the port) of outbound traffic so many private devices can share a single public IP address, routing return traffic back to the correct internal device.

questions.q: What does the "R" stand for in DHCP's DORA process?
options: Reset
Request — the client broadcasts that it will take the offered IP address
Route
Register
questions.explain: DORA stands for Discover, Offer, Request, Acknowledge — Request is the client broadcasting that it will accept the offered IP address.

questions.q: What is a rogue DHCP server?
options: A DHCP server that has run out of addresses
An unauthorized device answering DHCP requests with false information, which can redirect victims' traffic through an attacker-controlled gateway
A backup DHCP server used for redundancy
A DHCP server that only assigns IPv6 addresses
questions.explain: A rogue DHCP server is an unauthorized device that answers DHCP requests with false configuration — a real, documented attack technique that can redirect victims' traffic.

questions.q: What does DNS cache poisoning accomplish for an attacker?
options: It directly steals a user's password
It feeds a DNS resolver a false answer so victims are silently redirected to an attacker's server instead of the real one
It permanently disables DNS for the entire internet
It has no real-world security impact
questions.explain: DNS cache poisoning/spoofing feeds a resolver a false IP answer, silently redirecting victims to an attacker-controlled server instead of the legitimate one.

questions.q: In order, what happens when a laptop joins Wi-Fi, opens a browser, and loads a website?
options: DNS assigns an IP, then DHCP resolves the domain name, then NAT connects to Wi-Fi
DHCP (DORA) assigns an IP/gateway/DNS server, DNS resolves the site's domain name to an IP, then NAT rewrites the source IP as traffic leaves the network
NAT assigns an IP address, then DHCP translates the domain name
None of these services are involved in a normal web request
questions.explain: DHCP's DORA process configures the device first, DNS then resolves the typed domain name to an IP address, and NAT rewrites the outbound traffic's source address as it leaves the private network.
